corpus_scope: Stage 002 Kentucky homeowners — regulatory/statutory sources only (6 sources)
notes: Gold set derived from Phase 1 candidate evidence. Items here are reviewer-confirmed interesting, not legal findings. Smells 1, 3, 5 have no fixture examples because carrier policy forms are absent from this corpus slice.

items.fixture_text: refuse to pay a claim without conducting a reasonable investigation based upon all available information
items.reviewer_note: DOI Bulletin says insurers must conduct a 'reasonable investigation' without defining what threshold makes an investigation reasonable. This is the regulatory source for Smell 2 — carrier forms that mimic this language without defining the standard inherit the same ambiguity.

items.fixture_text: cannot reasonably justify the denial of a property insurance claim
items.reviewer_note: DOI states insurers cannot 'reasonably justify' denial without defining what justification threshold satisfies this. A carrier policy that defers claims decisions to an unversioned standard of reasonableness cannot be audited at time of loss.

items.smell_name: Calculation Rule Drift / Unversioned Rate Reference
items.fixture_text: specify the specific property conditions that are noncompliant with the insurer's underwriting guidelines
items.reviewer_note: DOI requires carriers to cite their underwriting guidelines when nonrenewing — but does not require those guidelines to be filed, versioned, or published. A carrier using unversioned internal guidelines to drive nonrenewal decisions is exposed to Smell 4: the calculation input (the guidelines) can change without notice or regulatory anchor.

KAR 806 KAR 13:150 references replacement cost in rate filing requirements. This is the regulatory definition anchor — carrier forms that use 'replacement cost' without citing this KAR provision or defining the calculation method are missing the anchor.

corpus_gaps.gap_reason: No carrier policy form or endorsement in corpus. Exclusion language ('including but not limited to', 'arising from or related to') does not appear in statutes or DOI bulletins — only in carrier-drafted policy forms. The KNIC SERFF filing (KY-SERFF-KNIC-127064322) is the next candidate source.

No carrier policy form or endorsement in corpus. Coverage-inversion patterns require a broad coverage grant followed by an exclusion that swallows it — this pattern only appears in insuring agreements, which are carrier-drafted form language.
